Gini's Mean Difference

Source: R/gini_mean_diff.R
gini_mean_diff.Rd

Estimates Gini's mean difference, the average absolute difference between two randomly chosen members of a population. It is a measure of spread on the scale of the data (like the standard deviation, but based on absolute rather than squared differences) and is the numerator of the Gini index.

Usage

gini_mean_diff(x, na.rm = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector with at least two observations. Any real values are allowed.

na.rm

Should missing values be removed before the calculation? Default TRUE. With na.rm = FALSE a missing value is an error.

Value

A single nonnegative number, the estimated Gini mean difference, in the units of x.

Details

The population quantity is \(\Delta = E|X_1 - X_2|\) for two independent draws. The estimate returned is the U-statistic $$\hat{\Delta}_n = \binom{n}{2}^{-1} \sum_{i < j} |x_i - x_j|,$$ the average of \(|x_i - x_j|\) over all pairs of distinct observations, which is unbiased for \(\Delta\). It does not change when a constant is added to every value. Kelley, Darku, and Chattopadhyay (2018, Example 7) name Gini's mean difference among the parameters covered by their general sequential procedure; Chattopadhyay and De (2016) use it to estimate the Gini index, \(\hat{\Delta}_n / (2 \bar{X}_n)\) (see gini_index).

References

Chattopadhyay, B., & De, S. K. (2016). Estimation of Gini index within pre-specified error bound. Econometrics, 4(3), 30. doi:10.3390/econometrics4030030

Kelley, K., Darku, F. B., & Chattopadhyay, B. (2018). Accuracy in parameter estimation for a general class of effect sizes: A sequential approach. Psychological Methods, 23(2), 226–243. doi:10.1037/met0000127

See also

gini_index, seq_aipe_gini

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Francis Bilson Darku fbilsond@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# Annual salaries (in thousands of dollars) of ten employees of a firm:
# two employees chosen at random differ by this much on average.
salary <- c(28, 31, 35, 38, 42, 47, 55, 64, 90, 170)
gini_mean_diff(salary)
#> [1] 42.04444

# The Gini index is the mean difference over twice the mean.
gini_mean_diff(salary) / (2 * mean(salary))
#> [1] 0.3503704
gini_index(salary)
#> [1] 0.3503704
